title: Cream-Filled Profiteroles with Chocolate Sauce
summary: Crisp choux buns filled with vanilla whipped cream, piled in a bowl and covered in a warm dark chocolate sauce.
equipment: 2 piping bags with 1 cm plain nozzles

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
dark chocolate (60-70% cocoa solids), finely chopped
ingredients.note: check the label for soya and milk

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Get ready
steps.text: Heat the oven to 220 °C (200 °C fan) and line the tray with baking paper. Beat the eggs and egg white together in the jug; you need about 120 ml, so discard any extra.

steps.title: Cook the paste
steps.text: Bring the butter, water, milk, sugar and salt to a full boil, then take off the heat and stir in the flour until the dough leaves the sides of the pan. Return it to low heat and cook for 3 min, smearing it against the pan, until it looks like shiny wet sand. Cooking dries the paste so it can absorb more egg and puff higher.

steps.title: Add the eggs
steps.text: Tip the paste into the processor and run it for 10 s to let steam escape. With the motor running, pour in the egg in a steady stream, then process for 30 s until smooth, glossy and sticky.

steps.title: Pipe and bake
steps.text: Pipe 24 mounds about 4 cm wide and 3 cm apart, then smooth any points with a wet finger. Bake for 15 min without opening the door, then turn down to 190 °C (170 °C fan) and bake for 8-10 min more, until golden and firm to the touch.

steps.title: Dry the puffs
steps.text: Cut a small slit in the side of each puff to let steam out. Put them back in the switched-off oven with the door propped open with the wooden spoon for 30 min, so the insides dry and the shells stay crisp, then cool on the rack.

steps.title: Fill
steps.text: Whip the cold cream, icing sugar and vanilla to soft peaks that just hold their shape. Pipe the cream into each cooled puff through its slit.

steps.title: Make the sauce and serve
steps.text: Bring the cream, golden syrup, butter and salt to a boil, take off the heat, add the chocolate and cover for 5 min before whisking smooth. Pile the puffs in the bowl and pour over the warm sauce straight away.

tips: A common mistake is taking the puffs out too soon; pale, soft shells collapse as they cool, so bake until golden and firm.
Do not open the oven door during the first 15 min, or the steam escapes and the puffs sink.
Fill the puffs just before serving so they stay crisp.
Unfilled puffs freeze well; recrisp them in a 150 °C (130 °C fan) oven for 8-10 min.
Don't taste the raw dough or batter: raw flour and raw egg aren't safe to eat until baked.
storage: Unfilled puffs keep in an airtight tin for 1 day or frozen for 1 month. Once filled, eat within 2 hours; keep leftover sauce in the fridge for up to 5 days and rewarm gently.
